bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility (cocoa, sugar, edible oils, packaging materials) — Management explicitly flags that volatility in these key input prices may adversely impact operating margins, and cites this first among the business risks the Company is exposed to. Confectionery inputs are commodity-linked, so this is a structural rather than one-off exposure.
- Intense competitive pressure from multinational, organised domestic and regional players — The MD&A states competitive intensity remained high across product categories with established multinational manufacturers, organised domestic players and regional brands competing; as a small listed confectioner the Company faces scale and brand-spend disadvantages.
- Shifting consumer preferences — Listed by management among its business risks. Consumers are moving towards premium offerings, innovative flavours and healthier alternatives, which puts an existing legacy portfolio at risk of relevance loss if innovation lags.
- Evolving food safety, labelling and packaging regulation — Management flags evolving regulatory requirements relating to food safety, labelling and packaging as influencing the operating environment; compliance changes carry reformulation, re-labelling and cost consequences.
- Profitability pressure and reduced debt-servicing capacity — The MD&A states FY 2025-26 was a challenging operating environment that impacted profitability, that the Company incurred a loss during the year, and that Debt Service Coverage declined because of lower operating profitability. Management describes the year as a transitional phase.
- Cost inflation and rising logistics costs — Increasing logistics costs and general inflationary pressure, together with changes in consumer spending patterns, are cited as continuing to influence the operating environment and margins across the sector.
- Macroeconomic, geopolitical and foreign-exchange exposure — Management notes geopolitical developments, global supply-chain disruptions, fluctuations in foreign exchange rates and changes in international trade policies may indirectly impact input costs and overall business operations. The Company has UAE and UK subsidiaries reporting in AED and GBP, adding translation exposure.
- Governance and control scale limits — The Board's Report notes Regulation 22 of the Listing Regulations (vigil mechanism) was not applicable to the Company during the year, indicating a compliance perimeter narrower than that of larger listed peers; the Company states it maintains a whistle-blower policy voluntarily and that internal controls are commensurate with the size and complexity of its operations.

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no named capex or expansion project, no commissioning or ramp-up timeline and no capacity addition. Expansion language is confined to intent: the Company states it 'continues to focus on improving operational efficiencies, strengthening its product portfolio, optimising manufacturing capabilities and identifying opportunities for sustainable long-term growth while maintaining financial discipline', and that it 'continues to evaluate opportunities for expanding its product offerings and strengthening market presence'. Management also cites 'better capacity utilisation' of existing assets rather than new capacity. The only structural corporate development in the year was financial, not physical: conversion of Convertible Warrants and Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds into equity, subdivision of shares and a bonus issue, described as strengthening the capital base. Geographically, the Company has established two wholly owned subsidiaries - Sampre Nutritions FZCO (Dubai Silicon Oasis Free Zone, UAE) and Sampre Nutritions Holding Limited (England, UK) - which extend its international footprint, though the AR attaches no investment plan or capacity to either.

outlook.body:
- Long-term outlook for the Indian confectionery industry remains positive, supported by favourable demographic trends, rising disposable incomes and increasing consumption
- Expanding organised retail and continued growth of digital commerce, including e-commerce and quick-commerce platforms, is widening consumer access to confectionery across metropolitan and emerging markets
- Consumer preferences shifting towards premium offerings, innovative flavours, healthier alternatives and convenience-based consumption, while value-priced products still account for a significant share of industry volumes in semi-urban and rural markets
- Raw material price volatility in cocoa, sugar, edible oils and packaging materials, plus rising logistics costs, is a stated pressure on operating margins
- High competitive intensity from multinational manufacturers, organised domestic players and regional brands across product categories
- The Reserve Bank of India projected real GDP growth of 6.5% for FY 2025-26, with external uncertainties described as elevated (Board's Report macro context)
